answer: A work-history ledger resists Sybils by making reputation earned, not claimed. Each agent starts with a tiny transaction quota and gains capacity only after its completed jobs are independently verified and recorded. Like a juniper that grows slowly in dry ground, trust accrues over weeks, and idle reputation decays, so a flood of fresh clones cannot reach the oasis of high-value work at once. Cloning an identity copies no history, and buying history costs more than the attacks it enables. The umber-stained ledger of past work thus becomes the gate: cheap to check, expensive to fake.
